engagement_background.objective: Reduce SaVida Health’s cost of purchased goods and services by roughly $240K–$470K through a six-month strategic sourcing program that leverages enterprise-wide purchasing power while preserving service levels and product quality, with quick-hit savings by year-end 2024 and full completion by March 2025.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Ten indirect spend categories representing approximately $5.3 million in annual spend are in scope (EMR, employee benefits, scientific/medical lab equipment & supplies, medical equipment & supplies, small parcel shipping, IT hardware, telecom, office supplies, commercial print, waste management). Low-spend or low-opportunity categories may be dropped after initial analysis; direct clinical service delivery costs are not included.
constraints_challenges: Supplier lack of responsiveness to data and usage requests
Potential supplier pushback and risk of uncontrolled side conversations, requiring a unified communication strategy
Limited or delayed participation from internal stakeholders for data provision, interviews, and approvals
Aggressive timeline to secure quick-hit savings by December 2024 and finish all workstreams by mid-March 2025
Incumbent supplier sensitivities that could complicate competitive bidding or negotiations
Gaps in historical line-item usage data, necessitating sampling and supplemental supplier data collection

procurement_environment.data_availability: Basic AP/PO and contract files exist internally, but detailed line-item usage data is often unavailable and must be requested from high-spend suppliers; no centralized contract or spend repository.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Historical usage data is incomplete; multiple follow-ups with suppliers are needed and both parties agree to accept partial data after reasonable effort.
